newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs bewail cuts in development aid.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs bewail cuts in development aid.

text.p: The European Union should divert to the world's poorest countries some of the funds it has allocated to its Mediterranean neighbours for 1997, Euro-MPs said on Tuesday.

British Socialist Glenys Kinnock told the parliament's development committee that the 15 percent cut which EU ministers planned to make in the bloc's external relations budget for 1997 was "appalling".
Aid to developing countries was at its lowest level since the early 1970s and 1.6 billion people were worse off now than 15 years ago, she said.
EU ministers plan to set an austere overall budget for 1997 which is only 2.2 percent higher than the 1996 budget.
Foreign policy expenditure, particularly development cooperation has taken a heavy blow to maintain this austerity, with some budget lines being cut as much as 22.5 percent.
The only exception to this trend is EU funding for the Union's Mediterranean neighbours, which is set to leap from 400 million European currency units ($500 million) this year to 800 million in 1997.

The development committee is demanding a string of amendments to the EU's draft budget, including the transfer of some 150 million Ecus from the so-called MEDA budget to poorer areas of the world, namely Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific.
The committee wants a further 20 million to be diverted to development projects carried out by non-governmental organisations.
